analysis.title: Precious Analyst: 2027 Outlook: It Is 2022 Again
key_insights: GS sees 2027 as a repeat of 2022 for precious metals: a rising Fed policy rate weighs on private investor demand, while structural central bank buying keeps a bid under gold.
Gold forecast is $4,650/toz by end-2027 (up 19% from spot, up 13% from the October average of $4,100/toz) and $5,600/toz by end-2028, driven mainly by central bank purchases.

GS economists expect a second Fed hike in December 2026 and a third 25bp hike in March 2027, which weighs on rate-sensitive Western ETF demand. Near-term downside risk and elevated volatility are expected while the Fed hikes.

Western ETF demand is expected to recover once the Fed cuts: four 25bp cuts between November 2027 and September 2028 take the funds rate to a terminal 3.25-3.5%. One 25bp cut adds about 60 tonnes of ETF demand spread over 6 months, and flows only turn once rates are actually lowered.

Macro-policy hedge demand (call-option demand) is assumed to decline toward its historical average as the hawkish Fed keeps debasement concerns contained. A return of that demand, for example on fiscal sustainability worries, is the main upside risk beyond $5,600 by end-2028.

Downside scenarios: four hikes and a higher terminal rate give gold at $4,585/toz by end-2027. A conservative lower bound assumes all ETF holdings above the rates-implied level unwind (about 300 tonnes of selling), giving $4,265/toz by end-2027.

Tactical risk: speculative COMEX positioning is at the 45th percentile and is expected to recover in the base case. Higher oil prices could trigger CTA selling, and sharp equity drawdowns (for example AI-cycle uncertainty) could initially pull gold lower through margin calls and deleveraging.

Gold did not rally during the 2026 Hormuz shock because it was a supply-driven inflation shock, as in 2022. Supply-driven inflation raises the risk of tighter policy and higher yields, which weigh on ETF demand. GS says gold's inflation-hedge role has not changed and that it is not a universal stagflation hedge.

Investor guidance: CTAs and macro hedge funds may find the next 3-6 months difficult for long positions. Longer-horizon investors seeking central bank demand exposure or a debasement hedge may find the current correction a more attractive entry point.

Central bank demand is treated as structural: 60 tonnes/month assumed through 2026-28 versus a 17 tonnes/month pre-2022 average. The seasonally adjusted 3MMA nowcast fell to 51 tonnes/month in September from 85 in August, and GS expects a recovery.

Central bank buying has risen about fivefold since 2022 after the freezing of Russian reserves. The base case assumes the trend continues for three more years. A World Gold Council survey found a record 45% of 76 central banks expect to raise their own gold reserves over the next 12 months.

China holds about 11.8% of reserves in gold versus about 80% for the US, Germany, France and Italy, and a global average above 20%. At about 20 tonnes/month it would take roughly three years to reach a 20% share. Risks to the 20% target are skewed to the upside because gold could support RMB internationalization.

Broader central bank gold selling is judged unlikely. Türkiye's reserve decline (129 tonnes) likely overstates outright sales because gold swaps show up as lower reported reserves. Gulf central banks hold low gold shares (UAE ~4%, Saudi ~8%, Oman ~5%, Qatar ~24%) and are more likely to liquidate Treasuries. DM central banks are debating where to store gold, not whether to sell.

Silver: the 2025/26 rally (peak above $120/toz) came from rising investor demand colliding with a London liquidity squeeze after tariff-driven inventory moves to the US. Price sensitivity rose to about 7% per 1,000 tonnes of weekly net demand versus about 2% normally. GS does not expect a repeat during the Fed hiking cycle.

GS expects gold to outperform silver in 2027 at least through the Fed hiking cycle, even with the gold-silver ratio near the top of its 45-80 historical range. Gold keeps the central bank bid that silver lacks.

Platinum and palladium: US Section 232 tariff uncertainty keeps supply fragmented and volatility elevated, but GS sees outright tariffs as unlikely and does not see this implying higher prices in 2027. Southern Africa supplies about 82%/46% of platinum/palladium and Russia another 11%/39%.

Platinum is more exposed to Fed hikes (larger investment component) and to European EV adoption (BEV sales in Europe +66% yoy in August 2026, implied ICE sales -10%), with defense spending as a partial offset. Palladium gets more support from hybrids (US hybrid sales +27% yoy in 3Q26, US BEV sales -45% yoy).

sector_views.rationale: Gold is expected to grind higher on central bank buying despite Fed hikes. Silver, platinum and palladium face headwinds from lower investment demand, and gold is expected to outperform silver in 2027.

trade_ideas.description: Long-horizon gold exposure, buying the current correction as an entry point (debasement hedge / central bank demand exposure)
trade_ideas.rationale: Structural central bank demand remains supportive and gold works as insurance against DM fiscal sustainability risks.
trade_ideas.risk: Further near-term downside from Fed hikes, an ETF unwind and CTA or deleveraging selling.

trade_ideas.description: Favor gold over silver through the Fed hiking cycle in 2027
trade_ideas.rationale: Fed hikes weigh on private investment demand for both metals, but only gold has the central bank bid, and a silver liquidity squeeze is unlikely during hikes.
trade_ideas.risk: Another silver liquidity squeeze, for example from renewed tariff concerns restarting US inventory building.

risk_factors: A more hawkish Fed (four hikes, higher terminal rate) would push gold lower, to $4,585/toz by end-2027.
A larger Western ETF unwind of about 300 tonnes would put gold at $4,265/toz by end-2027.
Speculative positioning can push prices away from fair value, and higher oil prices could trigger CTA selling.
Sharp equity drawdowns, for example AI-cycle uncertainty, could force margin-call liquidation of gold.
China central bank buying is a key pillar of the forecast, and a slowdown would hurt it.
Central bank gold sales by outliers (Türkiye, Kyrgyzstan, Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan, Russia, Venezuela) are possible but not expected to broaden.
Upside risk: a return of macro-policy hedge demand on fiscal sustainability concerns.
vol_and_positioning: GS expects elevated gold volatility and near-term downside risk while the Fed hikes.
Speculative COMEX gold positioning is at the 45th percentile, low, and is expected to recover in the base case.
Macro-policy hedge demand for gold, measured by call-option demand, is expected to fall toward its historical average.
Higher oil prices can trigger systematic CTA selling in gold, and sharp equity drawdowns can force deleveraging that pulls gold lower first.
Silver price sensitivity rose to about 7% per 1,000 tonnes of weekly net demand during the 2025/26 squeeze, versus about 2% normally.
Platinum and palladium volatility is expected to stay elevated because tariff risk fragments supply and reduces liquidity outside the US.
geopolitical: The 2026 Hormuz supply shock raised inflation without lifting gold, as in the 2022 Russian gas cut.
Russia's reserves were frozen, which started the fivefold rise in central bank gold buying since 2022.
US Section 232 tariff investigation on platinum and palladium, and silver's possible tariff eligibility via the critical minerals list, are driving metal inventories into the US.
Türkiye's central bank reserves fell 129 tonnes at the onset of the Middle East conflict and then rebounded, partly reflecting gold swaps.
France and the Netherlands have reportedly moved gold holdings away from New York.
Higher military spending and rising debt burdens in energy-importing countries are cited as possible triggers of fiscal sustainability concerns.

tension_points.bull_case: Structural central bank buying at 60 tonnes/month (versus 17 pre-2022) lifts gold to $4,650 by end-2027, and Western ETF demand recovers after Fed cuts, supporting $5,600 by end-2028. Macro-policy hedge demand returning would add upside.
tension_points.bear_case: Fed hikes weigh on rate-sensitive ETF demand. Four hikes give $4,585, and a 300-tonne ETF unwind gives $4,265. CTA selling on higher oil and equity-drawdown deleveraging could pull gold lower near term.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A larger ETF unwind (about 300 tonnes) or four Fed hikes with a higher terminal rate would break the $4,650 base case. A break in central bank buying would undercut the structural bid.

tension_points.bull_case: Silver could outperform because the gold-silver ratio is near the top of its 45-80 range.
tension_points.bear_case: Fed hikes weigh on investment demand for both metals but only gold has the central bank bid, and a silver liquidity squeeze is unlikely during hikes.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Renewed tariff concerns pulling silver from London into the US and restarting US inventory building would allow another liquidity squeeze.
